install.claude: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lennoxsaint/Skills.git && python3 Skills/scripts/skills.py install <skill-name> --host claude
install.codex: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lennoxsaint/Skills.git && python3 Skills/scripts/skills.py install <skill-name> --host codex
install.both: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lennoxsaint/Skills.git && python3 Skills/scripts/skills.py install <skill-name> --host both
install.update: git -C Skills pull && python3 Skills/scripts/skills.py install <skill-name> --host both --update

skills.name: claude-conductor
skills.summary: Run the Claude Code threads you already have as you: count every open thread, keep a ranked ledger, hand each owner a whole outcome and finish with proof.
skills.use_when: The user wants many existing Claude Code threads or projects moved to finished outcomes on their behalf ("conduct my Claude sessions", "run my projects as me", "move every open thread forward"). Not for one task in one session; for T3 Code use t3-code-conductor.
skills.try: Use claude-conductor: count every open thread in my projects, rank them against my goals, and move each one to a proven finish.
skills.requires: Claude Code; a thread or browser tool that can read your sessions

skills.name: t3-code-conductor
skills.summary: Turn one T3 Code thread into the conductor of all the others: census, roster, append-only ledger, outside review on a different model, and one phone review page of only the decisions that need you.
skills.use_when: The user runs agents in T3 Code and wants one thread to conduct all of them ("be my T3 conductor", "conduct my T3 threads", "set up a review desk for my agents"). Not for a single task; for Claude Code without T3 use claude-conductor.
skills.try: Use t3-code-conductor: be my conductor. Take a census of every T3 thread, give each lane a whole outcome, and keep one phone review page of what needs me.
skills.requires: T3 Code with its thread and delegation tools; Python 3.9+ for the desk helper

skills.name: adversarial-review
skills.summary: Have an independent reviewer critique a draft against a fixed rubric, check each finding, revise, and repeat until the bar is met or the budget runs out.
skills.use_when: The user wants a plan, answer, workflow, skill or implementation attacked by a second model before they rely on it ("adversarial review", "red-team this", "iterate until you both agree"). Not for a plain code review or for building the thing.
skills.try: Run an adversarial review of this plan with a 90/100 bar and an independent reviewer.
skills.requires: A second reviewer the agent can reach: another model's CLI or connector, or a fresh session of the same model

skills.name: ambitious
skills.summary: Run a big task the way the field's best practitioner would: find the goal behind the goal and the money moment, build from raw material, red-team it, get an outside judge and report against stretch targets.
skills.use_when: The user asks for exceptional effort ("go above and beyond", "max effort", "one-shot this") or says the stakes are high. Not for quick fixes or routine work.
skills.try: Go above and beyond: find where my signup page loses people and fix the biggest leak.
skills.requires: Node 18+ for the flight log and judge scripts; Codex CLI or Claude CLI for the outside judge

skills.name: email-triage-pro
skills.summary: Review Gmail, surface important mail, draft a small reply queue, and learn archive and writing preferences.
skills.use_when: The user wants their Gmail inbox reviewed: important mail surfaced, a few replies drafted, and archive and writing preferences learned from feedback.
skills.try: Use email-triage-pro to connect my Gmail accounts, surface important mail, draft a few replies, and learn from my feedback.
skills.requires: ChatGPT Gmail app, Claude Gmail connector, or gog 0.35+

skills.name: finish-work
skills.summary: Close a task with the right checks for its kind of work, an honest outcome summary and a written receipt.
skills.use_when: A substantive task is about to be called done, hits a checkpoint worth recording, or stops partial or blocked ("finish this", "close this out", "is it really done?"). Not for a quick answer or routine chat.
skills.try: Use finish-work to close this out: run the right checks, tell me what is proven, and write the receipt.

skills.name: goal
skills.summary: Turn a plan into a durable Codex goal packet or a concise Claude /goal prompt.
skills.use_when: The user has a plan, spec or task list and wants one bounded, steerable goal for a long agent run. Not for recurring routines or for writing the plan itself.
skills.try: Use goal to turn this plan into a durable goal: [paste the plan].
skills.requires: Python 3.10+ for Codex packet creation; no helper runtime for Claude prompt mode

skills.name: hill-climb
skills.summary: Turn real data into a locked answer key, then climb to a measured target with fresh agent sessions until the score and two outside judges say it is done.
skills.use_when: A long job must reach a quality bar you can prove: an eval score, a pass rate, or a design two outside judges would ship ("hill climb this", "build an eval and climb it", "keep going until it passes"). Not for quick polish of one draft: use loop for that.
skills.try: Hill climb this: build an answer key from my real logs, then climb until 90% of the cases pass.
skills.requires: Node 18+ and git; macOS sandbox-exec (the Linux bwrap path is untested); Claude Code or Codex CLI for the climber and the judges

skills.name: loop
skills.summary: Write a 100-point rubric for one draft, revise and rescore it, and stop at 100/100 or say exactly which points are missing.
skills.use_when: The user wants one local draft or artifact improved now with a score for every pass ("loop this", "make it 100/100", "iterate until perfect"). Not for long jobs that need a measured bar: use hill-climb for those.
skills.try: Loop this draft: make it 100/100 or tell me exactly what blocks it.
skills.requires: Nothing to install; the agent must be able to read and edit the draft

skills.name: save-10-percent
skills.summary: Audit recurring costs, verify actual use, find 10% in safe net savings, and optionally execute an exact approved batch.
skills.use_when: The user wants recurring costs or subscriptions audited against real use, with 10% in safe savings found and an exact batch to approve.
skills.try: Use save-10-percent to audit my recurring costs and find 10% in safe savings.

skills.name: strategy-prompt
skills.summary: Steelman every option, score them in a weighted matrix, recommend one, check that pick for bias and blind spots, then give a final recommendation.
skills.use_when: The user faces a business, strategy or research decision with real options and wants a rigorous recommendation ("strategy prompt", "steelman both sides", "score the options"). Not for a quick opinion or a pros and cons list.
skills.try: Use the strategy prompt: steelman both options, score them, and tell me which one to pick.
skills.requires: Nothing to install; a notes or web search tool helps when the agent has one
